messages:
maria: Thinking out loud — proposal to add a lightweight gateway rewrite shim to handle v1->v2 API consumers for up to 6 months. Goal: minimize client churn and buy time for SDK/library upgrades.

kevin: +1 to minimizing churn. what's the rough plan? header sniffing? body shape transforms?

maria: header sniffing + best-effort payload normalization. idea: client sets `X-Redwood-Client-Version` or we detect legacy field `prompt_text`. shim rewrites to new `input` shape and adds `compat-mode: v1` tag for telemetry.

sasha: Tradeoffs: simpler for users but increases O(1) latency on gateway. We need to quantify added p99. Also risk of ambiguous transforms (edge cases).

kevin: Agree. Also think about security: rewriting request bodies means more attack surface. Add strict validation rules and a toggle per-tenant.

nori: If we make this tenant-opt-in by default off, how do we onboard noisy customers? We need a clear opt-in flow (console flag + header opt-in) and a telemetry dashboard showing usage and errors.

maria: Opt-in + an automatic grace policy: if a tenant has  >90% of recent calls matching v1 shape, we can suggest opt-in via console + email. No automatic opt-in without human ack.

kevin: Implementation sketch: gateway middleware layer (Go) that runs a small rule engine. Pseudocode:```matchers := []{hasHeader("X-Redwood-Client-Version", "^v1"), hasField("prompt_text")}if any(matchers) { rewritePayload(); setHeader("X-Compat-Mode","v1"); emitMetric("compat.rewrites", 1) }```

kevin: Keep it bounded — limit transformations to a small whitelist of fields. No arbitrary JS templating.

sasha: How about fallbacks? If rewrite fails for a request, do we 400 or forward unchanged to v2 and log?

maria: Prefer: try rewrite, if rewrite validation fails then return 400 with a compat error code and a helpful message pointing to migration guide. But provide a debug endpoint for support to replay failed rewrites.

nori: Ops: we'll need per-tenant rate-limited logging so we don't DDOS S3 with bad payloads. Also add sampling for high-throughput tenants.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: gateway/compat-shim v1 -> canary pool (10% traffic) at 2024-11-07T14:30:00Z.

kevin: For telemetry, add tags: compat.mode, rewrite.success, rewrite.reason (enum). Also emit histogram for rewrite latency. That will let us detect latency regressions quickly.

sasha: Testing matrix: unit tests for each rewrite rule; integration tests with dummy legacy clients; golden files for edge cases (unicode, nested arrays). Also load test with real payload distributions.

maria: Rollout plan idea: 1) behind feature flag 2) internal canary 3) 10% customer canary (opt-in tenants) 4) broader opt-in with console prompts 5) sunset path communicated 6 months out.

nori: We should tie sunset to telemetry: once >95% of traffic uses v2 fields for 90d, we'll start a 60d deprecation countdown. Document in console.

kevin: Ops question: how do we prevent abuse where a client fakes header to get compat? We should only rewrite if payload shape actually matches legacy patterns, not only header.

maria: Agreed — require both header or client agent *and* payload heuristics. Also add a throttle: no more than X rewrites/sec per tenant.

sasha: One more: logs must include scrubbed payloads (PII) and a hashed request id to correlate replays without exposing data.

maria: Next actions: kevin to draft shim PR with tests + perf bench; sasha to write test matrix; nori to scope telemetry and console UX. I'll draft a short migration doc for support.

kevin: I'll include a small perf benchmark in the PR and baseline p95/p99 numbers.

nori: I'll prototype console opt-in UI flows and a migration email template.

maria: Nice. Tagging this thread for RFC follow-up. Thanks all :+1:
